subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept this positive-delivery approach for policy-active Codex turns, relying on Codex native PreToolUse delivery plus unified exec, or keep waiting for a different fail-closed/native-surface policy direction?
rationale: The patch is a security-boundary repair but intentionally changes Codex execution routing and thread reuse behavior, so automation can fix the code_mode_exec normalization gap but cannot choose the permanent runtime/compatibility policy.

options.title: Fix then review for merge
options.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` into the existing `exec` shell policy path, refresh against current Codex runtime behavior, and then do a maintainer security/compatibility review.

options.title: Prefer fail-closed direction
options.body: Keep this draft open only as source context and make the narrower fail-closed/canary path the canonical security fix.

options.title: Pause native delivery changes
options.body: Wait for an upstream Codex runtime contract that maintainers are ready to pin before changing OpenClaw policy-active routing.

recommendation.title: Fix then review for merge
recommendation.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` into the existing `exec` shell policy path, refresh against current Codex runtime behavior, and then do a maintainer security/compatibility review.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged native-hook bridge and are the strongest history match for the relay/security boundary.
